source_contract.second_class_scope_rule: All reviewed Chapter 2 locators are outside subsections explicitly marked 〔一等〕.

review_basis: current official MLIT 教則第5版 Chapter 2 source
answer correctness, answer uniqueness, distractor plausibility, commercial practice value, proposition/misconception/reasoning-path distinctness

decisions.rationale: 2.1.8(1) explicitly states potential criminal liability such as professional negligence causing death or injury. Existing accident questions test immediate response/reporting, not classification of the pilot's legal responsibility.
2.1.8(2) explicitly states potential Civil Code damages liability to victims. Existing insurance items test coverage scope, not the underlying civil obligation.

2.1.8(3) explicitly lists certificate cancellation/suspension, written warning and oral caution. Existing certificate coverage concerns renewal rather than sanctions for violation, misconduct or gross negligence.
2.1.7 explicitly requires route selection that prevents easy third-party approach. This preventive route-choice boundary is distinct from existing safety-margin and assistant access-management items.

2.2.1(1)1 explicitly requires planning that accounts for aircraft performance and pilot/assistant experience and capability. Existing planning items focus on external route/environmental hazards rather than mission-capability fit.

Tier B PASS. 2.2.1(1)3 separately names emergency landing locations and places where safe hovering/turning is possible. Q044 tests emergency landing-site availability and Q195 tests in-event landing priority; this candidate tests the preflight safe-holding/maneuvering branch before forced landing.

2.2.1(2)2 explicitly includes MSL altitude, obstacle locations and landmarks in site survey. Q185 concerns onsite obstacle confirmation for an automatic waypoint route; the broader vertical/geometric site-survey proposition remains distinct.

Tier B PASS. 2.2.1(2)4 explicitly requires preflight survey of pedestrian/vehicle traffic and manned-aircraft activity. Existing Q051/Q170 address encounter response or in-flight monitoring, so the flight-phase decision boundary is materially different.

2.2.3 explicitly requires collecting current weather, wind direction, warnings and advisories before flight. Existing items test weather-based decisions or in-flight deterioration, not this information-collection obligation itself.

2.2.7(1) explicitly links poor physical condition to distraction and reduced judgment. Existing human-performance questions separately test fatigue, stress and alcohol, so illness-related impairment is a new explicit proposition.

Tier B PASS. 2.2.7(2) explicitly states not to operate with sleep deprivation or accumulated fatigue. Q003 addresses flight-time management after fatigue develops during repeated operations; this item tests the pre-launch go/no-go branch when impairment already exists.
2.2.8 explicitly requires carrying the original or copy of permission/approval documentation for a specific flight. Q111 tests skill-certificate and flight-log carriage, not this document branch.

2.2.8 explicitly defines the oral-permission/no-document branch: the date and number must be answerable. This source-defined exception is not represented by Q111 or the Category II application timing question.

2.2.9(2) explicitly warns against overreliance on collision-avoidance equipment and specifically mentions birds. Q170 tests the general monitoring set; this item tests automation overtrust/residual-hazard reasoning and is commercially useful.

Q089 already requires preflight determination of pilot-assistant communication methods as part of assistant coordination. C015 changes the causal framing to misunderstanding/transmission delay but the answer-defining action and solving rule remain the same: predetermine the communication/information-sharing method before flight. This is too close under the 400-target quality floor and must not be retained as a wording/reason variant.

Tier B PASS. 2.2.10(3) explicitly distinguishes mandatory logging for specific flights from recommended logging for non-specific flights. Q042 tests the mandatory side; C016 tests the opposite statutory-versus-recommended boundary.
2.2.10(3) explicitly recommends recording inadequate risk responses for future flights. Existing log questions do not test capturing insufficient controls/near-miss learning evidence.

2.3.1(3) explicitly requires preserving flight logs for investigation and recurrence prevention. Existing accident items test immediate human safety, hazard prevention and reporting, not evidence preservation after those actions.

Tier B PASS. 2.3.2 separately defines immediate recipients based on event content—police, fire and other necessary agencies—together with MLIT reporting. Q052 covers stop/rescue/hazard-prevention and MLIT reporting but does not test recipient selection, so this branch is materially distinct.

Tier B PASS. 2.3.3 defines 25kg+ and Level 3.5 as independent OR conditions for sufficient third-party liability insurance. Q194 tests the 25kg+ branch; C020 uses <25kg and requires recognizing the separate Level 3.5 branch, a genuine source-defined boundary rather than number substitution.
